channel.title: # 🇱🇰 This Week in Sri Lanka
channel.description: Generated by gpt-5 from 303 English News Articles published between 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-24.

item.title: Central Bank held the Overnight Policy Rate at 8.75% as inflation drifted above target and external risks stayed elevated.
item.description: Policymakers noted headline prices rose 6.8% year-on-year in June and projected a gradual return to the 5% objective. They signalled vigilance over demand conditions while stating that May’s tightening would continue to filter through credit and spending. Officials highlighted a recent current account deficit since April alongside higher fuel import costs and softer tourism earnings. Gross reserves stood at $6.45 billion at end‑June, while the currency stabilised in recent weeks after earlier policy measures. The Board cited renewed Middle East tensions and global commodity moves as upside risks to prices. It reaffirmed readiness to act to keep inflation anchored around the target and support medium‑term growth.

item.title: Brent crude briefly crossed $100 a barrel, reviving cost and external pressures.
item.description: The benchmark price touched a two‑month high after Red Sea tanker incidents and later eased but remained elevated. A sustained rise would lift import bills and could widen trade gaps if tourism receipts and remittances do not offset higher energy outlays. Domestic price pass‑throughs to transport and LPG have historically raised living costs. The central bank flagged the oil move as a risk to its near‑term price path in its latest review.

item.title: Japan sought interest on delayed compensation for the cancelled Colombo LRT project.
item.description: Authorities confirmed three payments were made in 2024—JPY 189.7 million on 23 August, US$ 1.031 million on 27 August, and Rs. 108.7 million on 24 September. Tokyo later requested interest, and a committee is now reviewing the claim. Cabinet terminated the rail scheme on 24 September 2020 after officials deemed it not cost‑effective. The move has left residual financial issues with contractors and consultants that remain under examination.

item.title: Health authorities capped lab charges during the dengue surge as clinicians urged early care over vaccination.
item.description: Regulators reminded private providers that a Full Blood Count with report must not exceed Rs. 400 and the NS1 antigen test Rs. 1,200. Complaints can be lodged via the 1977 hotline with receipts for enforcement. Clinicians reported 78,125 infections and 56 deaths so far this year, with 162 MOH areas at high risk. Specialists advised immediate treatment for warning signs and said a vaccine is not a solution to the current wave.

item.title: Government set out plans to lift the renewable share above the current 70% target and reinforce the grid.
item.description: Officials said they would upgrade the Sampur–Kappalthurai line from 300 MW to 600 MW and construct four additional transmission systems. The President also called for investment in a Northern 400 kV (kilovolt, a unit of electric potential) backbone to carry more variable power.

item.title: President ordered tighter protection of fast‑developing coasts and faster delivery of human‑elephant conflict projects.
item.description: A steering committee will oversee coastline works, with an expert panel tasked to report on erosion at Oluvil. The Environment Ministry reviewed a Rs. 19,719 million portfolio and was told to finish funded mitigation projects within the year.

item.title: Fisheries agencies mapped 2027 priorities and relief after Cyclone Ditwah.
item.description: Sector leaders reviewed harbour upgrades at Myliddy, Gandara and Rekawa and rehabilitation at Karainagar. A Rs. 189 million programme to replace boats and nets for affected families is underway alongside plans to raise exports and local supply.

item.title: Police probed the abduction and killing of a foreign national after a clash at a waterfront development.
item.description: Investigators recovered a body hidden under stones in Karandana, Eheliyagoda, and seized a vehicle believed to have moved the victim. Two suspects were arrested at the airport while attempting to depart, and consular officials requested a full inquiry.

item.title: A new daily rail service will connect the capital with Thalaimannar Port.
item.description: Train No. 5003 will leave at 03:50 and arrive at 10:44, with the return, No. 5004, departing at 04:10. The rake will serve major Northern Line stations and offer two air‑conditioned first‑class coaches with reserved seating.

item.title: The national passport rose to 94th in the 2026 Henley Index.
item.description: The ranking improved from 96th in 2025 and 2024, compared with 100th in 2023 and 102nd in 2022. The index rates travel documents by visa‑free and visa‑on‑arrival access across 227 destinations (a methodology that counts entry without prior permits).
